body.tou_shift: Moving {{share}}% of its day-tariff energy to the night tariff saves money. It does not reduce CO₂: Kosovo's grid factor is an annual average.

methodology.factorBody: {{value}} kg CO₂e per kWh · {{source}} · reference year {{year}} · {{methodology}}.

caveats.lifecycle: Lifecycle factor: Ember applies standard lifecycle values per fuel, not measurements from Kosovo's lignite plants. GHG Protocol Scope 2 reporting often uses combustion-only factors; the two differ.
caveats.generation: Generation-based: it describes electricity generated in Kosovo; imports and exports are not reflected.
caveats.annual: Annual average: it does not change by hour, so moving load to the night tariff saves money but not CO₂e.

methodology.scope1: Scope 1: fuels you burn (generators, forklifts, heating). Declared by you.
methodology.scope2: Scope 2: the electricity you buy. Location-based = metered kWh × the grid factor.
methodology.mv: Each action is checked against an adjusted baseline (28 days before, by day type) with a 90 % confidence interval — IPMVP-inspired, Option B. Not a certified M&V.
methodology.coverage: Machines on EnergyFlow meters account for {{share}} of the main incomer over the last 30 days.
methodology.simulated: This is a fictional demo company. Its machines are simulated (with real Pristina weather and the official Kosovo tariff); the methods are the ones used for real meters.

scan.subtitle: Use your camera to check an electricity bill, read a meter or a nameplate, and capture fuel receipts.
scan.privacy: The photo is sent to Groq (an AI service) only to read the text, and isn't stored. You check and can correct every value before anything is saved.

check.supplier_universal: Issued by {{name}}, Kosovo's universal service supplier.
check.supplier_licensed: {{name}} appears in ERO's register of electricity supply licences.
check.supplier_unknown: “{{name}}” isn't among the electricity suppliers EnergyFlow knows from ERO (2022 register and later decisions). Check it at ero-ks.org.
check.supplier_differs: Your tariff in EnergyFlow is with {{tariff}}, but this bill is from {{bill}}.
check.date_in_future: The date {{date}} is in the future.
check.period_reversed: The billing period ends before it starts.
check.period_unusual: The billing period is {{days}} days long; monthly bills usually cover 28–31 days.
check.period_in_future: The billing period ends on {{date}}, which hasn't come yet.
check.issued_before_period_end: Issued on {{issue}}, before the period ends ({{end}}).
check.due_before_issue: The due date is before the issue date.
check.kwh_sum_wrong: Day + night ({{sum}}) doesn't equal the total ({{total}}).
check.meter_backwards: The current meter reading ({{end}}) is lower than the previous one ({{start}}).
check.meter_diff_ok: The meter readings match the consumption ({{diff}}).
check.meter_multiplier: The meter readings × {{factor}} (a current-transformer meter) match the consumption.
check.meter_diff_wrong: The meter readings differ by {{diff}}, but the bill charges {{kwh}}.
check.money_sum_wrong: Amount ({{net}}) + VAT ({{vat}}) doesn't equal the total ({{total}}).
check.vat_rate: VAT is {{rate}}, Kosovo's rate for electricity.
check.vat_rate_wrong: VAT is {{rate}}, but electricity in Kosovo is taxed at {{expected}}.
check.metering_not_covering: EnergyFlow wasn't measuring yet for the whole period, so the kWh can't be compared.
check.metered_diff: Billed {{billed}}, measured {{metered}} ({{diff}}). Small gaps can come from loads EnergyFlow doesn't meter or different reading days.
check.metered_diff_large: Billed {{billed}}, but EnergyFlow measured {{metered}} ({{diff}}). Ask the supplier whether the reading was estimated.
check.tariff_match: The price matches the official tariff: {{billed}} billed, {{expected}} expected ({{diff}}).{{note}}
check.tariff_diff: {{billed}} billed against {{expected}} expected at your tariff ({{diff}}).{{note}}
check.tariff_diff_large: {{billed}} billed against {{expected}} expected at your tariff ({{diff}}): the prices don't match the official tariff.{{note}}
check.tariffAllHigh: (No day/night split on the bill, so all kWh were priced at the high tariff.)
check.already_saved: A bill for {{month}} is already saved; saving replaces it.
check.first_reading: First reading: the next one will be compared with what EnergyFlow measures in between.
check.reading_backwards: The reading ({{reading}}) is lower than the previous one ({{previous}}).
check.too_soon: Less than an hour since the last reading: too early to compare.
check.meter_matches: Since the last reading the meter advanced {{meter}}; EnergyFlow measured {{metered}} ({{diff}}).
check.meter_differs: The meter advanced {{meter}}; EnergyFlow measured {{metered}} ({{diff}}). Small gaps can come from loads EnergyFlow doesn't meter.
check.meter_differs_large: The meter advanced {{meter}}, but EnergyFlow measured {{metered}} ({{diff}}). Check that every circuit is metered.
check.hp_kw_mismatch: {{kw}} kW and {{hp}} HP on the plate don't match (1 HP = 0.7457 kW).
check.nameplate_consistent: Consistent: voltage, current and cos φ give an electrical input of {{input_kw}}, so efficiency ≈ {{efficiency}}.
check.nameplate_inconsistent: The rated {{kw}} doesn't fit the electrical input of {{input_kw}} from voltage, current and cos φ: check the values.
check.ie_class_low: Efficiency class {{class}}. In the EU, new motors of 0.75–1000 kW must be at least IE3 since July 2021 (Regulation (EU) 2019/1781): worth considering when it's replaced.
check.running_above_rating: {{code}} often runs at {{p95_kw}}, {{load}} of this rating: check the plate belongs to this machine.
check.oversized: {{code}} typically runs at {{p95_kw}}, only {{load}} of its rating. Motors running far below their rating work less efficiently.
check.load_ok: {{code}} typically runs at {{p95_kw}}, {{load}} of its rating.
check.rated_power_changes: Saving changes {{code}}'s rated power from {{old}} to {{new}}.
check.fuel_unknown: Choose the fuel: diesel, petrol, gas oil, LPG or heating oil.
check.scope1_factor: Scope 1: {{co2_kg}} at {{value}} kg CO₂e per litre (UK DESNZ 2025 factors).
check.label_old_scale: Energy class {{class}} is on the old A+++ scale; since 2021 the EU has been moving labels back to A–G.
check.label_class_unreadable: The energy class “{{class}}” couldn't be read.
check.label_cost: At your electricity price this costs {{eur}} and emits {{co2_kg}} per {{unit}}.

score.title: EnergyFlow Score
score.howTitle: How the EnergyFlow Score is calculated
score.howIntro: A weighted average of six parts, each 0–100, over the last {{days}} days. Every part comes from your measurements.
score.scaleNote: The scales (e.g. waste at 25 % of consumption scores 0) are EnergyFlow's design, not an industry standard. Parts without data are left out of the average.

definition.waste: Quantified waste as a share of consumption; 0 at 25 %.
definition.schedule: Energy used outside their schedules by machines that should be off (critical loads excluded); 0 at 20 % of consumption.
definition.health: Share of consumption from machines without an open efficiency-drift or failed Turn Off alert.
definition.peak: Load factor (average ÷ peak 15-minute power); 100 at 60 % or more.
definition.follow_through: Opportunities acted on, and alerts resolved within 24 hours (last 30 days).
definition.coverage: Share of the main incomer metered per machine × completeness of the 15-minute data.

detail.health_one: {{count}} machine with an open issue ({{share}} of consumption)
detail.health_other: {{count}} machines with an open issue ({{share}} of consumption)
detail.followThrough: {{acted}} of {{opportunities}} opportunities acted on · {{resolved}} of {{alerts}} alerts resolved within 24 h

flow.title: Energy flow this month
flow.unmeteredHint: Measured at the main incomer but not by a machine meter (lighting circuits, sockets, losses).
flow.aria: Energy flow this month: {{kwh}} from the grid, of which {{waste}} waste.
flow.note: Waste is what EnergyFlow's detectors quantified (after hours, idle, efficiency drift); everything else a machine used counts as productive.

alertDetail.title: Alert
alertDetail.overloadAdvice: The machine drew {{pct}} of its nameplate power. Running above the rating overheats motors and wiring: check for a jam, a seizing bearing or a blocked filter before it runs again.
alertDetail.rule: Each minute's peak is compared with the machine's own normal peaks: robust z = (peak − median) ÷ (1.4826 × MAD). A spike is z > {{z}} in at least {{min}} consecutive minutes and ends after {{clear}} normal minutes. It is critical when a reading exceeds {{overload}} % of the nameplate rating.
alertDetail.baseline: Normal for {{slot}}: median peak {{median}}, MAD {{mad}}, from {{samples}} 15-minute periods while running ({{from}} – {{to}}).
